title: Probabilistic Residual Correction of Issued Photovoltaic Forecast Profiles Without Plant Metadata
content: Photovoltaic forecasting studies often assume access to plant metadata and numerical weather predictions. A downstream energy manager may instead receive only an issued production trajectory and recent measurements. This study tests whether this trajectory can be corrected without coordinates, capacity, orientation, or forecast weather. The EMSx data provide energy measured every 15 minutes and vendor forecasts for 70 anonymised systems. Complete daily profiles spanning 24 hours are formed, using chronological training, tuning, calibration, and test partitions. The test contains 8,898 profiles and 854,208 matched deliveries. A global LightGBM model predicts residuals from the vendor trajectory, calendar variables, causal measurements, and recent forecast error. It reduces pooled mean absolute error from 71.34 to 52.18 kWh and improves all 70 systems. Most of the gain appears when the complete issued profile is added. Causal rolling calibration improves the grid continuous ranked probability score from 38.62 to 35.85 kWh and raises central 90% coverage from 0.827 to 0.919, although the weighted interval score changes from 48.91 to 49.24 kWh. After limited EMSx adaptation, the strongest foundation model variant, Chronos-2 with the vendor trajectory, reaches test MAE 61.34±0.11 kWh across 32 seeds. The residual correction retains lower test MAE.
